answer:
Based on my research, the Canadian coin with the highest mintage rate in 2013 according to the Royal Canadian Mint was the **one-dollar coin (Loonie)**, with an estimated production of approximately **120-170 million pieces**.

The **primary image on the reverse (back side)** of this 2013 Loonie is the **common loon**, a large North American aquatic bird that gives the coin its nickname. 

This iconic reverse design features:
- A profile illustration of the loon facing right
- Created by engraver Robert-Ralph Carmichael
- Used since 1987 when the Loonie replaced the one-dollar banknote
- The loon is shown above the word "CANADA" at the bottom edge

Among all Canadian circulation coins in 2013, the Loonie had significantly higher production numbers than quarters (~17 million), dimes (~17 million), half-dollars (less than 1 million), or pennies, making it by far the most frequently minted denomination that year.

steps.text:
Based on my research, the Canadian coin with the highest mintage rate in 2013 according to the Royal Canadian Mint was the **one-dollar coin (Loonie)**, with an estimated production of approximately **120-170 million pieces**.

The **primary image on the reverse (back side)** of this 2013 Loonie is the **common loon**, a large North American aquatic bird that gives the coin its nickname. 

This iconic reverse design features:
- A profile illustration of the loon facing right
- Created by engraver Robert-Ralph Carmichael
- Used since 1987 when the Loonie replaced the one-dollar banknote
- The loon is shown above the word "CANADA" at the bottom edge

Among all Canadian circulation coins in 2013, the Loonie had significantly higher production numbers than quarters (~17 million), dimes (~17 million), half-dollars (less than 1 million), or pennies, making it by far the most frequently minted denomination that year.
